per_response.derivation: Input cannot exceed the documented 1,050,000-token model context window; output is bounded separately by the documented 128,000-token maximum. Their sum is a deliberately loose per-response upper bound, not a typical response length.
per_response.applicability: Conditional on the captured subscription provider honoring the documented limits of the same gpt-5.5 model. The frozen run and rollout profile must match; this is not an API generation experiment.
per_response.input_cap_not_used: The local Codex catalog's effective context/compaction budget is not treated as a hard upstream request-token ceiling. The historical 386,400 response bound is not reused.

cardinality_rule.name: isolated_normal_response_tail
conditions: Exactly one local typed-RPC turn/start, matching interrupt, completed directive message and interrupted turn completion.
The response segment starts after the prior same-thread cumulative usage barrier or at turn start.
All pre-directive user/reasoning/agent items pair exactly; exactly one agent message completes; no tool boundary, foreign concurrent turn or unsupported protocol event occurs.
After the directive there is at most one unfinished reasoning/agent item and no fresh cumulative usage. Resumed-output grace requires that one unfinished item.
Every nonexact grace decision has the supported output-resumed or timeout outcome and the inventory count agrees with the strict observer's missing-usage error.
cardinality_rule.scope_limit: The rule bounds the isolated normal tool-loop tail conditional on complete visibility of model-response and tool boundaries. It is not an unconditional bound against opaque upstream retries, subresponses or hidden auxiliary provider work. It is not a rule for arbitrary interrupted turns. Unsupported shapes retain an unknown upper bound. Raw completion records cannot silently clear the missing tail.

formulas.workflow_upper: recorded_lower + sum(proven_missing_response_count * 1178000); null if any missing tail lacks the cardinality proof
formulas.ineligible: Any non-accounting capture error, unsupported model/profile, inconsistent usage or mismatch between strict observer and gap inventory.
formulas.quality: All saved implementation outcomes are scored separately with the frozen canonical scorer; one pair cannot establish quality equivalence or sampling confidence.
